posts.title: This geneticist’s age-reversal tech could help restore sight
posts.summary: Yuancheng (Ryan) Lu is obsessed with aging. And with eyes. As he steps outside the Whitehead Institute in Cambridge, Massachusetts, his aviator glasses darken automatically in the sun. Age-related blindness runs in his family. A great-aunt in China, the story goes, was killed crossing a road because she couldn’t see oncoming traffic. And Lu’s own…
bullets: Geneticist Yuancheng Lu has pioneered a reprogramming gene therapy that successfully restored optic nerve function in mice by reverting cells to a youthful state.
The therapy, now designated as ER-100, has officially entered human clinical trials, with Life Biosciences administering the first treatment to a glaucoma patient in June.
This development marks a major milestone in rejuvenation science, transitioning from theoretical laboratory research to human therapeutic application for age-related vision loss.
The success of this trial could validate the broader field of epigenetic reprogramming, potentially opening new investment and therapeutic pathways for treating degenerative diseases.

posts.title: This founder is teaching chips how to recycle (their energy)
posts.summary: Throughout the history of the computer chip, engineers have treated waste heat as an inevitable cost of a calculation. Hannah Earley, however, thinks it’s a design choice. Earley, 31, is cofounder and chief technology officer of Vaire Computing, a startup building chips that recycle energy usually thrown away as heat—a strategy known as reversible computing.…
bullets: Vaire Computing is developing 'reversible computing' hardware designed to recycle energy typically lost as waste heat during standard chip calculations.
The startup has achieved a technical milestone by creating a resonator that recovers more energy than it consumes, providing proof-of-concept for a 50-year-old theoretical approach.
By retaining information during intermediate computational steps rather than erasing it, the technology aims to significantly improve energy efficiency in data centers and consumer electronics.
While the technology is currently in an early stage, it represents a potential paradigm shift in semiconductor design that could address the thermal and power constraints of modern computing.

posts.title: This AI entrepreneur is developing agents that can plan ahead for the unexpected
posts.summary: Danijar Hafner’s office in San Francisco’s SoMa district sits mostly empty. His brand-new startup is still in stealth mode and doesn’t even have its name on the door. On the day I visit, there’s only one other person there, and little in the way of furniture. But what it lacks in decor, it makes up…
bullets: Danijar Hafner’s stealth startup is leveraging model-based reinforcement learning to enable AI agents to navigate and plan within previously unseen physical environments.
The company utilizes 'world models' to simulate physical reality, allowing robots to learn and predict outcomes without the need for extensive real-world trial-and-error training.
This approach aims to solve the generalization problem in robotics, enabling humanoids to operate effectively in dynamic, unfamiliar spaces like private homes.
The technology represents a significant advancement in autonomous systems, potentially reducing the development time and safety risks associated with deploying robots in human-centric environments.

posts.title: Xiaomi delivers 30,153 cars in August, down 17.15% year-on-year
posts.summary:
Xiaomi Auto's deliveries rose 9.65% in the first 8 months, reaching 44.8% of its 550,000-unit annual target.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi Auto delivered 30,153 vehicles in August, marking a 17.15% year-on-year decline and the second consecutive month of sequential delivery decreases.
With only 44.8% of its 550,000-unit annual target met through August, Xiaomi must achieve a monthly average of 75,881 deliveries over the final four months to reach its goal.
To stimulate growth, Xiaomi has entered the extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) market with the new Sky Nomad series, which saw over 10,000 locked-in orders within four minutes of launch.
The company faces significant headwinds as it enters the EREV segment, which has seen a 15.85% year-on-year decline in retail sales during the first eight months of the year.

posts.title: BMW's Neue Klasse iX3 electric SUV appears in China filing ahead of November deliveries
posts.summary:
Pre-orders are open for the China-specific long-wheelbase Neue Klasse iX3, with prices starting at 269,900 yuan ($39,810).
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BMW has filed for the China-specific long-wheelbase Neue Klasse iX3, which features a 235 kW motor and CATL-supplied lithium iron phosphate batteries.
The vehicle is built on BMW's dedicated Neue Klasse electric platform and includes a 3,005 mm wheelbase, providing a 108 mm increase over the standard version to enhance rear-passenger space.
The model integrates advanced local technology, including a driver assistance system developed with Momenta and an infotainment suite supporting Huawei HiCar and Alibaba's AI large language models.
Pre-orders are currently open with prices ranging from 269,900 to 339,900 yuan, with official deliveries scheduled to commence in November.
